facts.raw_span: A 65-year-old man with benign prostatic hyperplasia
prostate-specific antigen level was 0.796 ng/mL
Uroflowmetry revealed reduced urine flow, prolonged micturition time, and obstructive findings
He was started on oral Alfuzosin 10 mg once daily
loss of appetite and malaise, followed by generalized pruritus, dark urine, and jaundice
He denied use of aspirin, acetaminophen, or herbal medicines
no history of liver disease
leukocyte count 5.8 K/μL
total bilirubin 7.6 mg/dL (0.2–1.2)
Abdominal ultrasonography showed normal liver, gallbladder, common bile duct, and intrahepatic bile ducts

support_spans: loss of appetite and malaise, followed by generalized pruritus, dark urine, and jaundice
contradict_spans: He denied use of aspirin, acetaminophen, or herbal medicines
concepts.why: The patient developed jaundice and elevated liver enzymes after starting Alfuzosin, suggesting a drug-induced liver injury.

contradict_spans: Serologic tests for HBsAg, anti-HBc IgM, anti-HCV, anti-HAV IgM, anti-HEV, HEV RNA, and HCV RNA were negative
concepts.why: The patient has elevated bilirubin levels, but negative serologic tests for viral hepatitis make this diagnosis less likely.

contradict_spans: Autoimmune markers (ANA, AMA, ASMA, LKM-1) were negative
concepts.why: The patient has elevated liver enzymes, but negative autoimmune markers make this diagnosis less likely.

contradict_spans: Abdominal ultrasonography showed normal liver, gallbladder, common bile duct, and intrahepatic bile ducts
concepts.why: The patient has elevated bilirubin levels, but normal ultrasonography and no other signs of PBC make this diagnosis less likely.

contradict_spans: Abdominal ultrasonography showed normal liver, gallbladder, common bile duct, and intrahepatic bile ducts
Magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography demonstrated a normal biliary anatomy
concepts.why: The patient has elevated bilirubin levels, but normal ultrasonography and MRCP make this diagnosis less likely.

contradict_spans: Metabolic evaluations—including transferrin saturation, ferritin, alpha-1 antitrypsin, ceruloplasmin, 24-hour urinary copper, and ophthalmologic exam for Kayser–Fleischer rings—were normal
concepts.why: The patient has elevated bilirubin levels, but normal metabolic evaluations and no Kayser-Fleischer rings make this diagnosis less likely.
It explains the finding of normal liver, gallbladder, common bile duct, and intrahepatic bile ducts on abdominal ultrasonography in the context of jaundice.

frontier_selector.why: The temporal relationship between the initiation of Alfuzosin and the onset of liver injury symptoms, such as loss of appetite, malaise, generalized pruritus, dark urine, and jaundice, decided it.
